name: Tag input
description: A field that turns what you type into removable chips: tags, labels, email recipients. Enter or a comma adds one, pasting a comma-separated list adds them all, Backspace in the empty field removes the last. Optional suggestions open under it as you type, like a Combobox.

classes.ayy-tag-input: Root: looks like an .ayy-input, holds the chips then the input, and grows to more lines as needed. Clicking its empty space focuses the input. With suggestions add ayy-combobox and put an .ayy-combobox__listbox inside.
classes.ayy-tag-input__tag: A tag, on an .ayy-chip.ayy-chip--removable <span data-value> with its .ayy-chip__remove button (aria-label "Remove design").
classes.ayy-tag-input__input: The borderless <input type="text"> after the chips; the field's id, label and aria-describedby go on it.

default.looks: An Input-like wash field with a line-strong border, holding removable chips and a text box that grows onto more lines as tags are added.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a click puts the caret in the text box.

focus.looks: A 2px ring around the whole field; each chip's × has its own. Forced colours: Highlight.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor. Disable the chips' × buttons too.

selected.looks: The suggestion under the arrow keys gets Combobox's wash; suggestions that are already tags are aria-disabled.

error.looks: A destructive border (and ring while focused). Say why in a FieldError.

loading.none: No loading look in the field. While suggestions load, show the Combobox's "Searching…" row.

open.looks: Suggestions open under the field like a Combobox's list.

scale.sm: At least the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
scale.md: At least the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: At least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), more padding, lg text.

sizes.density: The first line's height follows data-density (above); each line of tags adds a chip's height.

js: splitTags(text) → tags split at commas and new lines; addTags(values, add, { max?, caseSensitive? }) → values with the new ones appended (no duplicates, ignoring case); tagChip(value, removeLabel?) → a chip element; tagInputClass({ size?, suggestions? }); tagRemoveIcon (SVG markup). connectTagInput(root, { name?, max?, caseSensitive?, onChange?, removeLabel?, addedText?, removedText? }) → { values, setValues, destroy } wires plain markup and draws the chips.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-tag-input and makes it work: it draws a chip for each added tag (chips already in the HTML are the starting tags), keeps one hidden input per tag for forms, wires the suggestions listbox if there is one, and announces each change. The values property reads and sets the tags.

attributes.name: Form name: a hidden input per tag carries it.
attributes.case-sensitive: Keep tags that differ only in case apart.

events.ayy-change: { values } — every tag, after one is added or removed.

TagInput.renders: <div class="ayy-tag-input"> chips + <input class="ayy-tag-input__input"> (+ a listbox with suggestions); other props go on the input, className on the root

props.suggestions: string[] — known tags listed as you type; added ones show disabled
props.emptyText: ReactNode — in the suggestions list when nothing matches. Default "Press Enter to add it"
props.name: string — a hidden input per tag

a11y: Label the inner input with <Label htmlFor> on its id and describe how to add a tag in a FieldHint ("Press Enter or type a comma").
Each chip's × is a real button named "Remove design"; Backspace in the empty field removes the last tag too.
Adding and removing are announced in a polite live region ("design added"), and focus stays in the input.
With suggestions the input is a combobox: arrows move through them, Enter adds the highlighted one, and ones already added are aria-disabled.
do: Use it for a short open list of free text: tags, labels, keywords, email recipients.
Offer the tags people already use as suggestions so they don't create near-duplicates.
Set max when there's a limit, and say it in the hint.
Check each tag (an email address) in onValueChange and show a FieldError for a bad one.
dont: Don't use it to pick from a fixed set — use Checkbox chips (Chip) or a multi-select list.
Don't use it for a single value — use an Input or a Combobox.
Don't colour tags by meaning without a word for it.
